notes: F1 disposition: resolved, alternative accepted. S1 now fixes the domain by host and OS user with a state root derived from account identity; cwd, checkout, TUI, HOME, XDG, and ptest env variables cannot silently select another root, and conflicting overrides fail visibly, so the capacity-multiplication path is closed. A same-domain nested executing invocation returns 75/nested-invocation before queueing with live ancestry validation, which removes the budget-1 parent/child deadlock while keeping read-only inspection usable. The sole alternate domain is an explicit per-invocation fixture option on a newly created private directory, labeled isolated-fixture-domain in every output, excluded from normal evidence, and not activatable by env or repo config. A2 and A4 carry the env-only-cannot-create-a-domain and nested-cannot-deadlock negative cases. This is narrower than my suggested general isolated-domain mechanism and is acceptable; the enforceable contract is the explicit option plus visible label plus private new directory, while the sentence that the harness never uses user suites is harness policy rather than a ptest-enforced rule, which is fine for a product contract.

F2 disposition: resolved, alternative accepted. T3, the new fallback-table row, and C3 now state one semantic for relevant inputs changing during an automatic run or explicit full gate: outcome incomplete, reason changed-during-run, full_gate_eligible false, no baseline, final status 70 when the runner returned zero, and the runner's actual nonzero code preserved otherwise, with runner_exit_code recorded separately. T3 defines declared non-input outputs (coverage output, result files, runner caches declared by a supported adapter or reviewed policy, only when they supply no assertions, selection, configuration, or runtime behavior) whose routine writes do not invalidate a run, and A5 requires the positive fixture. The author rejected my exit-0 recommendation and rejected exempting runner-requested snapshot/golden updates. Neither choice violates an explicit user constraint: AGENTS.md's preserve-exit-status rule is honored because the raw runner code is separately recorded, child streams are untouched, ptest-owned codes were already part of the legacy contract, and the original C3 already permitted a nonzero operational status on a green child. The changed-expectations policy follows the user's correctness-before-speed and safe-invalidation priorities and is explicit rather than silent. Non-blocking observation: the repaired T3 paragraph dropped the original phrase 'retain its actual failures' for the changed-during-run case. T4 ('failed and errored tests remain mandatory') and A6 ('failure obligations survive ... incomplete reports') still cover it, so I could not trace a failure path, but restoring one clause in T3 stating that observed failures from an invalidated run are still recorded as obligations would remove any reading that an incomplete run's failures are unattributable.

F3 disposition: resolved, alternative accepted. C1 separates display from execution: default ptest-owned output exposes only runner kind, mode, adapter-generated options/grants, argument count, and provenance, withholding all arbitrary configured or caller-supplied argv including executable paths and option-looking tokens, so the policy is testable with distinct sentinels and needs no secret-name recognition. Error paths follow the same policy. The explicit reveal option on where and init --dry-run is labeled unredacted-command-disclosure, off by default, incompatible with prompt/history/status export, never persists raw argv, and never dumps environment values. The Exposure row and A8/A11 now specify sentinel fixtures in a URL, unknown option, positional argv, option-looking token, and executable path, and honestly retain raw runner streams, OS process argv, user-named test IDs/paths, and intentional reveal as residual surfaces. This withhold-all approach differs from my deny-list suggestion and is stricter and more testable. The usability cost (redacted init dry-run preview and migration preview by default, exit-127 and unknown-option errors that cannot name the token) is a preference, not a violation of any user constraint, and the reveal option is the documented mitigation.

Clarification notes: N1 (legacy habit changes, initialization-required exit 2, also_roots, status exit 0) resolved in P2/P4/A1 and consistent with C3 inspection semantics. N2 (SIGINT/SIGTERM trigger, process-group delivery, parent-only SIGKILL leaves charged capacity, cancel command deferred) resolved in S4/A3. N3 (child cwd is the resolved project root in the active checkout, no argv rebasing) resolved in C1/A11. N4 (bundled guide via ptest guide, optional non-overwriting docs/ptest-agent.md export, pointers only to existing targets) resolved in CLI table, section 9, A13. N5 (one runner per project config, ambiguous root fails) resolved in P2/A1. N6 (doctor priority order, honest discovery-limit reporting, finite explicit higher budget) resolved in D1/A8. N7 (declared reservation for arbitrary wrappers) parked with rationale; I labeled it a preference and accept the parking. N8 (coverage failure cannot seed a baseline and remains a full-gate obligation) resolved in T3/T4/A5 and consistent with the no-tests-needed row. N9 (legacy bundle outside NG admission, drain before relying on the ceiling) resolved in P4/A1. N10 acknowledged with no scope added. Minor wording inconsistency, not a defect: the P2 pre-initialization availability list names static doctor, previews, help, and status but omits guide, while section 9 and A1 state guide works before init.

No tests, benchmarks, or commands were executed; this is a read-only documentation review. The applied spec text matches .pipeline/out/spec-repair.diff hunk for hunk.
